name: Kempinski Dresden - Hotel Taschenbergpalais
insider_take: Sleeping inside a rebuilt royal palace steps from Dresden's Zwinger — this is Saxon history wrapped in five-star luxury.
whats_special: The Taschenbergpalais was originally built in the early 18th century by Augustus the Strong as a gift for his favorite mistress, Countess Cosel. Destroyed in the devastating 1945 Allied bombing of Dresden, the palace lay in ruins for decades before being meticulously reconstructed and reopened as a Kempinski hotel in 1995. Today, it stands as one of Germany's most historically significant luxury hotels, occupying a prime position between the Dresden Frauenkirche and the legendary Zwinger Palace complex. Guests of The Kempinski Club 1897 enjoy elevated perks including exclusive lounge access and bespoke concierge services befitting the hotel's royal pedigree.
pro_tip: Request a room or suite facing the Zwinger courtyard for a truly cinematic Dresden view — especially magical when the palace is illuminated at night. Club 1897 members should take full advantage of the private lounge for an unforgettable evening tasting of Saxon wines.
dont_miss: Just steps from the hotel, the Zwinger Palace houses world-class museums including the Old Masters Picture Gallery (Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister). The nearby Semperoper opera house is one of Europe's finest — book tickets well in advance. And don't leave Dresden without a stroll along the Brühlsche Terrasse , the so-called "Balcony of Europe" overlooking the Elbe River.
